# Results -- Study 265 (IPO-Volume) on the real annual tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Recipe: pair the
hardcoded annual US operating-company IPO count (Jay Ritter / University of
Florida) with the S&P 500 calendar-year **price** return (Shiller index level,
dividends excluded). Standardize the IPO count with an expanding, past-only
window (the "froth z-score"), then regress the **next-year** S&P return on it
with Newey-West HAC standard errors. The folklore -- "a flood of IPOs rings the
bell at the top" -- predicts a **negative** slope. One-year execution lag (the
position for year Y+1 is set from data fully observed by year-end Y).
As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Shape | Fingerprint (fwd_return) |
|--------|--------|-------|--------------------------|
| Ritter IPO counts (hardcoded) x Shiller S&P 500 price (`_cache/shiller_sp500.parquet`) | 1980 -> 2024 (signal years) | 41 forecastable years | `a6855574f53b` |

The IPO series excludes closed-end funds, REITs, ADRs, unit offers, SPACs, and
sub-$5 penny offerings. S&P returns are **price-only** (Shiller index level).

## Primary specification (predictive regression, HAC errors)

`fwd_return = alpha + beta * froth_z + eps`

| Quantity | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Slope **beta** (per 1 sigma of froth) | **-0.0019** |
| **HAC *t*** on beta | **-0.07** |
| R^2 | 0.000 |
| Predictive corr(froth_z, next-year return) | -0.011 |
| n (years) | 41 |

The slope is **statistically indistinguishable from zero** (HAC *t* = -0.07). On
the full real tape, IPO volume carries **no** forecast power for the next year's
S&P return. The folklore's sign (negative) is right in spirit but the magnitude
is a rounding error.

## The coincidence trap -- why the myth feels true

| Correlation | Value | Reading |
|-------------|-------|---------|
| **Contemporaneous** corr(froth_z, *same-year* return) | **+0.317** | IPOs flood the market *during* good years |
| **Predictive** corr(froth_z, *next-year* return) | **-0.011** | froth tells you nothing about next year |

IPO volume is a *coincident* indicator of euphoria, not a *leading* one. The
1999 flood (476 IPOs) coincided with a +20% S&P year; the bust came two years
later, by which point IPO volume had already collapsed on its own. The eye
remembers the famous tops (1999-2000, 2021) and forgets that the timing never
actually lines up one year ahead.

## Sub-period slope -- a data-mining warning, not a result

| Period | beta | HAC *t* | n |
|--------|------|---------|---|
| 1985-1999 | -0.007 | -0.19 | 15 |
| 2000-2012 | -0.159 | -2.11 | 13 |
| 2013-2024 | -0.207 | **-6.23** | 12 |

The two recent windows *look* like the folklore working, and the 2013-2024 slice
even hits *t* = -6.2. But these are **n ~ 12** slices carved out of a sample where
the full-period slope is zero -- a textbook subsample mirage. The 2013-2024 result
is driven by the 2021 SPAC flood -> 2022 drawdown coincidence plus a handful of
quiet-IPO/strong-return years; it does not survive into an honest full-sample test.

## Tradability -- the long/flat froth-timing rule loses to buy-and-hold

Rule: be **long** the S&P next year when this year's froth z < 0 (the IPO window is
not wide open), **flat** otherwise. Long-only (no short, no borrow). 5 bps one-way
cost on each switch.

| Book | Mean/yr | Vol | HAC *t* | Hit rate |
|------|---------|-----|---------|----------|
| Strat (gross) | +8.34% | 14.0% | +4.12 | 0.59 |
| Strat (net, 5 bps) | +8.33% | 14.0% | +4.12 | -- |
| **Buy & hold** | **+10.79%** | 15.8% | +4.68 | 0.76 |
| **Strat net - Buy&hold** | **-2.46%/yr** | -- | **-1.12** | -- |

The rule was long in 29 of 41 years, switched 9 times (45 bps total cost drag),
and still **trailed buy-and-hold by -2.46%/yr**. Sitting out the "frothy" years
mostly means sitting out good years -- exactly what the coincidence trap implies.

## Positive control -- the engine is honest

On the deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_annual`) the same estimator
recovers a planted slope and reads ~zero on the null:

| Planted beta | Recovered beta | HAC *t* |
|--------------|----------------|---------|
| 0.00 (null)  | -0.004 | -0.36 |
| -0.06 (froth)| -0.056 | **-4.92** |

So the flat real-tape result is a **true null**, not a broken regression.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** Full-sample predictive HAC *t* = **-0.07** (n = 41), far
  below the *t* >= 2 inference bar. The contemporaneous +0.32 correlation is a
  coincident-not-leading artifact; the negative sub-period slopes are *n* ~ 12
  mirages. The positive control confirms the engine would detect a real slope if
  one existed. Verdict: **NONE**.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** The tradable long/flat wrapper **underperforms
  buy-and-hold by -2.46%/yr** (net of 5 bps costs); going flat in frothy years
  forfeits good years. There is nothing to capture. Verdict: **MIRAGE**.
- **Sample-size honesty.** n = 41 forecastable years is tiny; even the positive
  result we *could* report (recent sub-periods) is the kind of subsample fishing
  the desk exists to flag.
